goal: pom.xml uses Spring Boot 3.x and Java 17; nothing under src uses the javax.persistence, javax.validation, javax.annotation or javax.servlet packages; no spring.factories file is left; and `mvn -B test` passes with every existing test migrated to JUnit 5 and actually run (none deleted, skipped or disabled).
final_message:
The project is now on Spring Boot 3.2.12 and Java 17. `mvn -B test` passes: 4 tests run, 0 failures, 0 skipped. I didn't run the application itself, only the tests.

- **`pom.xml`:** The parent is now 3.2.12 and `java.version` and the compiler source/target are 17. I removed the JUnit 4 dependency. JUnit 5 comes in through `spring-boot-starter-test`, and Surefire picked it up.
- **`javax.*` to `jakarta.*`:** I changed `persistence`, `validation`, `annotation` and `servlet` across all the main sources. A grep finds no remaining imports from those four packages.
- **Tests:** Both test classes now use `org.junit.jupiter.api.Test`, `@BeforeEach` and `Assertions`. I also swapped the argument order in the one `assertNotNull` call, because JUnit 5 takes the message last. No tests were deleted or disabled.
- **`spring.factories`:** Deleted, along with the empty `META-INF` directory.

Some stale text is still there. The `pom.xml` comments and `<description>` still say "Spring Boot 2.7", and a comment in `LegacyCustomerApiApplication.java` still says "javax.* era". I left them alone because none of them affect the build.

Deleting `spring.factories` has two effects:
- **`WebConfig`:** It is a `@Configuration` in the application's own package, so component scanning still picks it up.
- **`FeatureProperties`:** It was listed there as an `ApplicationListener`, which it isn't, so that entry didn't do anything useful. Nothing else registers it now. It also has no `@Component`, `@EnableConfigurationProperties` or `@ConfigurationPropertiesScan`. I left it that way because you asked for no business-behavior changes.

One more thing in `WebConfig`: `loggingFilter` builds a `FilterRegistrationBean` without setting a filter. I didn't touch it, but I haven't checked whether the app starts with it as written.
reason: migrated cleanly: compiles, tests pass, no javax, no spring.factories
